author: reek
body: The manifest-scope pin. The compiler emits each program's capability manifest into the CDX header, and until now that emission was verified only by inspection: nothing inside a guest can read its own manifest, so a regression in manifest-cap-bytes was caught by no test.

author: reek
body: This is a battery test. It needs the subject built by the compiler under test rather than a frozen image, which is what the `.disk-src` sidecar is for: it names manifest-subject, and the battery attaches that test's fresh CDX as this one's disk. Until that sidecar existed the pin was real and ungated -- it sat skipped with a shell script beside it, which is a test nobody runs. build/manifest-pin-test.ps1 remains for pointing the pin at some OTHER compiler.

author: reek
body: Checked by sabotage, against the defect it was written for: making manifest-cap-direction answer readwrite unconditionally, as it once did, moves both entries here and nothing else. That regression handed a program declaring [FileSystem.Read] a READWRITE filesystem capability in its own manifest, and no test in the tree could see it.
